# `s2_security_groups` — version 1.4

Source: `presets/security-group-models/s2-security-groups.satz`

## Purpose

The S2 security group model: S1's five admin groups plus a distinct
NETWORK ADMINS group, and the org-level grants split accordingly. In S1 the
network authority is folded into project-admins (compute.networkAdmin,
compute.xpnAdmin — "Hybrid Connectivity administrators … Network
administrators" in their description); S2 carves it out so a network team
can own VPCs, Shared VPC, firewalls, DNS and connectivity without the
project-admin power over everything else, and project-admins lose exactly
those two network roles. Everything else is S1 unchanged.

Groups and grants in ONE file (typed sections beside the estate's own):

To adopt groups that already exist in the tenant:
satz adopt <estate> --only google_cloud_identity_group --execute
Memberships are NOT part of this pack: presets define groups,
humans grant membership.

The first admin holds Project Creator and Billing Account Creator explicitly — the two
roles a new organisation grants its whole domain. Once that grant and the groups' are
live, `satz apply` takes the domain off those two roles and touches nothing else of the
organisation's policy; `satz plan` says what the apply would do.

The project admins' roles are the list param `gcp_project_admins_roles`; its default is the
list the grant below reads, `roles/owner` included — the horizontal reach over every project,
present and future, that the platform team holds while business units hold vertical roles on
their own folders and projects. An estate that wants that reach PAM-grantable binds the param
to `roles/writer` (every service's write permissions in every project — Google's basic role
that Privileged Access Manager grants and a condition bounds, which Owner cannot be) together
with `roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin`, `roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin`,
`roles/resourcemanager.projectDeleter` and `roles/billing.projectManager` — what Owner gives
beyond Writer — and the rest of the list; the plan then shows two destroys and four creates.
The API and gcloud grant Writer; the console cannot. ADR 0090.

Required from the estate: customer_domain, first_admin, svc_iac_account, infra_project_name

## Use it

```
params {
  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  gcp_organization_admins_name = "gcp-organization-admins"
  gcp_project_admins_name = "gcp-project-admins"
  gcp_network_admins_name = "gcp-network-admins"
  gcp_security_admins_name = "gcp-security-admins"
  gcp_security_viewers_name = "gcp-security-viewers"
  gcp_billing_admins_name = "gcp-billing-admins"
  gcp_project_admins_roles = [
    "roles/resourcemanager.folderViewer",
    "roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin",
    "roles/resourcemanager.tagAdmin",
    "roles/iam.organizationRoleViewer",
    "roles/iam.serviceAccountCreator",
    "roles/owner",
    "roles/bigquery.admin",
    "roles/pubsub.admin",
    "roles/cloudsupport.admin",
    "roles/compute.viewer",
    "roles/container.viewer",
    "roles/monitoring.admin",
    "roles/logging.admin",
    "roles/logging.configWriter",
    "roles/logging.privateLogViewer",
    "roles/monitoring.viewer",
    "roles/billing.user",
  ]
}

use "presets/security-group-models/s2-security-groups.satz"
```

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `customer_domain` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `first_admin` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `infra_project_name` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `svc_iac_account` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

**gcp_organization_admins_name** — The address is the group's identity: renaming it later means a new group, every member moved by hand and every role re-granted. This group holds the organisation's highest roles.


**gcp_project_admins_name** — The address is the group's identity: renaming it later means a new group, every member moved by hand and every role re-granted.


**gcp_network_admins_name** — The address is the group's identity: renaming it later means a new group, every member moved by hand and every role re-granted. S2's reason to exist: the network authority carved out of project admins.


**gcp_security_admins_name** — The address is the group's identity: renaming it later means a new group, every member moved by hand and every role re-granted.
